title: A derived complete module annihilated by a finitely generated ideal modulo that ideal is zero

standard_prerequisites.name: A cokernel of a map between derived complete modules is again derived complete, so the truncated quotient considered in the proof inherits derived completeness
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the contradictory inverse limit computed at the end impossible, since a derived complete module has vanishing derived limit.

standard_prerequisites.name: An endomorphism of a derived complete module that is surjective has nonzero inverse limit only in the zero case, i.e. an inverse system given by a surjective self-map with nonzero target contradicts derived completeness
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the contradiction from the surjectivity of multiplication by the next generator on the truncated quotient.

core_obligations: Assume that the quotient of the module by the ideal vanishes and write the ideal as generated by finitely many elements (proof lines 26112-26113).

Choose the largest index for which the quotient of the module by the ideal generated by the first few generators is nonzero; if no such index exists the module itself is zero, which is the conclusion, so suppose it exists and denote that nonzero quotient (proof lines 26113-26115).
Observe that this quotient is derived complete because it is a cokernel of a map between derived complete modules (proof lines 26115-26118).

Use the maximality of the index to see that multiplication by the next generator is surjective on that quotient, and conclude that the displayed inverse limit is nonzero, which contradicts derived completeness and finishes the proof (proof lines 26118-26120).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a maximal partial quotient of the module by the first generators (proof lines 26112-26115).
Note that this quotient is derived complete as a cokernel (proof lines 26115-26118).
Derive the contradiction from the surjective multiplication on that quotient (proof lines 26118-26120).
difficulty_reason: The statement is the module-level derived Nakayama lemma: a derived complete module with respect to a finitely generated ideal that vanishes modulo that ideal is zero (statement lines 26099-26110). The proof argues by contradiction: it picks the largest index for which the quotient of the module by the ideal generated by the first few generators is still nonzero, notes that this quotient is derived complete as a cokernel of a map between derived complete modules, and uses maximality to see that multiplication by the next generator is surjective on it, so that the displayed inverse limit is nonzero and derived completeness is contradicted (proof lines 26112-26120). The maximality argument and the resulting surjectivity are the substance of the proof. It is the module-level companion of the lane's card on the derived Nakayama lemma for objects of the derived category; the counted span needs the one same-chapter reference carried as a navigation stub.
